planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in well-drained, slightly acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade to morning sun; new-growth purple color is most pronounced with a few hours of direct sun.

directions: Purpureus is a false holly selection grown for new spring foliage that emerges deep purple-black before gradually maturing to dark green through the summer, giving a seasonal color shift on top of the spiny, holly-like leaf texture typical of the species. Like other Osmanthus heterophyllus cultivars it produces tiny, sweetly fragrant white flowers tucked among the leaves in fall, easy to miss by eye but obvious by scent, and it forms a dense, deer-resistant, evergreen screen or informal hedge with minimal maintenance. Plant in well-drained, slightly acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade to morning sun, sheltered from the harshest afternoon exposure, and prune lightly to shape only after fall bloom.

common_name: Mrs. Schiller's Delight Viburnum (Dwarf Dense Walter's Viburnum)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist to average, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Mrs. Schiller's Delight stays even more compact and dense than Little Joe, making it useful for a very low, tightly clipped hedge or edging.

directions: Mrs. Schiller's Delight is one of the smallest and most tightly compact selections of native Walter's viburnum, forming a dense, fine-textured mound of small, glossy, semi-evergreen to evergreen leaves that stays well under 3 feet without regular shearing. Clusters of small white flowers open in spring, followed by small red fruit ripening to black that draws songbirds, on a plant scaled for low hedging, edging, and small foundation beds where even Little Joe would eventually need trimming to stay in bounds. Like other Walter's viburnum selections it tolerates a range of soil moisture, from average garden conditions to occasionally wet sites, and needs little pruning to hold its naturally tidy, rounded form.

common_name: Black Magic Camellia (Near-Black Deep Red Camellia)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 5.5-6.5), humus-rich soil in partial shade; Black Magic's unusually dark flower color shows best against the shrub's own dark glossy foliage in a shaded setting rather than bright, washed-out light.

directions: Black Magic is a camellia japonica selected for exceptionally deep, dark red flowers that read as nearly black-red in low winter light, among the darkest flower colors available in the genus, held in a semi-double to formal double form on an upright, medium-sized evergreen shrub. It blooms in mid-to-late winter through early spring, providing dramatic, saturated color in the landscape at a season when little else is flowering, and its dense, glossy dark-green foliage provides a fitting backdrop for the equally dark blooms. Grow in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade, mulch to keep roots cool and moist, and prune lightly to shape only right after flowering, since next season's buds set over the following summer.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 5.5-6.5), humus-rich soil in partial shade; Tama Beauty's flower pattern can vary somewhat from bloom to bloom, part of the charm of many peppermint-striped camellia cultivars.

directions: Tama Beauty is a camellia japonica prized for its semi-double flowers streaked and flecked in rose-pink over a white background, a lively peppermint-candy pattern that stands out from the solid-colored blooms of most camellia cultivars, with prominent golden stamens at the center. It flowers in mid-to-late winter into early spring on a compact, well-branched, glossy-leaved evergreen shrub, providing weeks of color during the coldest part of the year when little else in the garden is blooming. Grow in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade, mulch to keep roots cool, and prune only lightly to shape right after flowering, since flower buds for the following season set over the summer.
